clue.text: Coo! Perhaps it is time to put on ring

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one thing on another sets it in front, so the first piece leads

blocks.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, time inside
to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise that it is time to put a ring on, perhaps a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' reads as a British exclamation of surprise, but with 'Perhaps' it is an example of the sound a pigeon makes. Bird, meaning time served in prison, is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon's coo is one example of the noise a feathered creature makes, hence the 'Perhaps' signalling an example.

clue.text: Gathering with hostility in cave

indicators.note: 'with ... in' sets one item inside the other, the second holding the first

blocks.note: a bee is a gathering for shared work or fun, as in a sewing bee
war is open hostility

explanation.surface: A hostile meeting held inside a cave, like a gang of troglodytes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' is not a hollow in rock but the Latin imperative 'beware!', once used as schoolboy slang for a lookout's warning. The 'in' at the end belongs with 'with' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cave is Latin for 'look out', an old British public-school warning call, so it matches the English command exactly.

clue.text: Deliver clarification on penalty

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: An official explaining a penalty decision, as a referee might after a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clarification' suggests explaining something, but here it means clearing a liquid of impurities, as when sugar or oil is purified.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarifying a substance means purifying it of sediment, which is exactly the industrial process of making something purer.

clue.text: Isolate copper, in contact with fluorine repeatedly

indicators.note: something done repeatedly happens more than once, so the element symbol is written twice

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to can mean touching, as in cheek to cheek
F is the chemical symbol for fluorine, taken twice

explanation.surface: A chemistry instruction to separate copper that keeps touching fluorine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a lab procedure, and 'Isolate' fits chemistry so well that it hides as the definition. 'in contact with' gives a small connecting word, as in face to face.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate a place or person is to sever them from others, the sense of a town severed by floods.

clue.text: At Centre, valet is catching Wooster purloining last of garden rakes

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letter is kept
to catch something is to hold it, so one piece wraps around another
a thief purloining an item takes it in, so one piece ends up holding the other
the last of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: the middle of the five letters of valet
taken as written
Bertie Wooster is P G Wodehouse's hapless gentleman, served by the valet Jeeves
the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: A valet catches Bertie Wooster pinching garden rakes from the middle of the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rakes' look like garden tools beside 'garden', but they are dissolute men. The valet and Wooster evoke Jeeves, yet the valet only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is an old word for a dissolute pleasure-seeker, which is precisely what a debauched man of loose morals is.

clue.text: Minority backing a little Conservative chap following probes

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so these letters are read from right to left
a probe pushes inside something, so these letters go into the other piece

blocks.note: a wet is a moderate, soft-line Tory, a little Conservative rather than a hardliner
a chap is a he
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A small group supporting a minor Tory man who conducts investigations.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a 'wet' is a moderate Conservative, the term Thatcher's allies used for her less hardline colleagues. 'backing' sounds like support but turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A minority is a small number of people, and the phrase names any small select group as opposed to the many.

clue.text: Impetuous folk stop TV show’s interruptive material

blocks.note: ho is a call to stop or halt
the advertisements are what interrupt a commercial TV show

explanation.surface: Rash people trying to stop the commercials that break into a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' looks like a verb acting on the TV show, but it gives only a short call to halt; the rest of the clue describes the commercial breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetuous people act rashly without thinking, which is the meaning of this word for quick-tempered, reckless types.

clue.text: American university academic merging upcoming pre-Congress activities

indicators.note: when two things merge they run into each other, so one letter crosses into the other piece
in a down clue, coming up means travelling from bottom to top, the opposite of the usual reading

blocks.note: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut
prof is short for professor

explanation.surface: An American academic combining the events leading up to a session of Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: The word's final E slips inside the academic's title before the whole is read upwards. 'Congress' looks political but means sexual intercourse, so the definition is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress is a formal word for sexual intercourse, so the activities preceding it are the kissing and caressing beforehand.

clue.text: Good health points effecting switch in what paper shops do

indicators.note: a switch swaps two things over, so the two letters trade places in the phrase

blocks.note: S and W are compass points, south and west
a newsagent's business is selling newspapers

explanation.surface: A health-promotion scheme that changes what newsagents do.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that opens the selling phrase and the W ending it change places. A paper shop is a British newsagent, which sells newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good health is a state of physical and mental soundness, which this modern lifestyle term names.

clue.text: Female we bet I will spoil with love

definitions.text: Female we bet I will spoil with love

indicators.note: spoiling something wrecks its original form, so the letters end up rearranged

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, written O

explanation.surface: A man boasts that he will pamper his female partner with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a fiancée is the woman her groom promises to spoil with love, the wedding theme of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancée is a woman engaged to be married, someone the groom will indulge with affection after the ceremony.

clue.text: Substance secreted by oleasters, side by side

indicators.note: something secreted is concealed within, so only an inner run of letters is kept and the rest falls away
things placed side by side sit next to each other, so the shrub's name is written twice in a row

blocks.note: the tail of the first copy of the shrub's name, its opening four letters dropped
the head of the second copy, written next to the first, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: A botanist describing a substance produced by oleaster shrubs growing next to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secreted' sounds biological, as plants do secrete substances, but here it means hidden. Oleaster is a shrub, the Russian olive. Write it twice in a row and the answer straddles the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterols are a class of organic compounds, such as cholesterol, so the general word for a chemical material fits.

clue.text: Cycle around Herts town in the direction of Iron Age settlement

indicators.note: to cycle round is to rotate, so the front letter moves to the back

blocks.note: Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire, England
heading for a place means going towards it

explanation.surface: A bike ride around a Hertfordshire town heading for an ancient earthwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' reads as riding a bicycle but it moves the first letter to the end. Herts is the standard abbreviation for Hertfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring fort is a circular fortified enclosure built by prehistoric peoples, an example of an ancient defended settlement.

clue.text: Writing on edge of pot

indicators.note: in an across clue, placing a word on another sets it after, so the second piece follows

blocks.note: a hem is the finished edge of cloth
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: An inscription around the rim of a ceramic pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' looks like a vessel, but it is cannabis, the plant also known as hemp; 'of pot' is an adjective phrase meaning made from that plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis, which is the hemp plant, so an adjective meaning made from hemp fits.

clue.text: Was sorry about adopting writing system with no ‘B’ mechanism

indicators.note: having none of something means it has been taken away
to adopt is to take in, so one piece is housed inside the other
turning about faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: rued means regretted
Braille is the raised-dot script read by touch by blind people
the letter itself, quoted, to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone regretting adopting a script that lacks the letter B.
explanation.walkthrough: The regret word turns round, then takes in the tactile writing system minus its initial. The quoted 'B' looks like a grade but is just the letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: A derailleur is the gear-changing device on a bicycle that moves the chain between sprockets, an example of a mechanism.

clue.text: Start of briefing is not as in agenda: answer party with opening issue at table

definitions.text: party with opening issue at table

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, the only one used
'X not Y in' means one thing stands where another used to be inside a word

blocks.note: the opening letter of briefing
agenda with each of its two As, read as the word 'as', replaced by an I for 'is'
ans is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A meeting where the agenda was departed from, a party arguing over an issue at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'as' are read as plural letters: two Is in place of two As. In Swift's Gulliver's Travels the Big-Endians are the faction who crack their boiled eggs at the big end.
explanation.definitionFit: The faction's whole quarrel is over which end of a breakfast egg to break, an opening issue at the table.

clue.text: Reason a trip to the tobacconist is on and off?

definitions.text: Reason a trip to the tobacconist is on
definitions.note: a whole situation stands for the two-word phrase, fair because 'snuff out' read literally describes running dry of snuff

blocks.clueFragment: Reason a trip to the tobacconist is on
blocks.note: first meaning: having run out of powdered tobacco would send a user to the shop
second meaning: to off someone is slang for killing them, extinguishing a life

explanation.surface: Someone wondering why a planned visit to the tobacconist keeps being on, then off again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' looks like one phrase meaning intermittently, but it splits: the first meaning ends at 'on', and 'off' is slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, it is the state of having no powdered tobacco left; as a phrasal verb it means extinguish or kill.

clue.text: Lovers – bonkers – at it again indoors

indicators.note: bonkers means crazy, so the letters go wild and are reordered
being indoors means inside a building, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: more of something is it again
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazed couple who are at it again inside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at it' is British slang for having sex, which fits the lovers; in the wordplay it is just four letters to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoretti are cupids, the little winged figures of love in Renaissance art, so the plural for sweethearts fits.

clue.text: Ways to engage with a model

indicators.note: gears engage by meshing, so these pieces lock between the others

blocks.note: two ways: ST for street and RD for road
and means with or plus
taken as written

explanation.surface: Methods of getting involved with a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ways' looks like methods, but it is two abbreviated thoroughfares, a street and a road, which split to hold the linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a benchmark or exemplar against which others are measured, the same sense as an ideal pattern.

clue.text: After heated clashes with many, agree fixture for big match

indicators.note: things that clash collide and jumble, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After angry disputes among many people, a date is agreed for a big football game.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'big match' sounds sporting but is a wedding, a match between two people; agreeing its date is the traditional phrase for setting a wedding date.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix the date of a wedding is the idiom, and a marriage is a match, so the big match is the ceremony.

clue.text: Admitting Arts Academy deserted very fine composer

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for deserted
v is the abbreviation for very
OK means fine
the RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London

explanation.surface: An arts academy abandoned after admitting a very fine composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitting' sits at the start but applies to the last word: fine holds the Academy. D for deserted is a cricket and records convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonín Dvořák was the Czech composer of the New World Symphony, an example of a classical composer.

clue.text: Plant U-turning keeps of course wasting energy

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so a letter drops away
turning round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: U means upper-class in British usage, the same as posh
yes and of course both agree
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A plant making a U-turn while staying on course and running out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U-turning' is split: U is the old British label for upper-class speech and manners, and 'turning' reverses its synonym. E is the physics symbol for energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic herb of the mint family, an example of a garden plant used in cooking and medicine.

clue.text: Planted smackers on breasts, so reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how it is spoken

blocks.note: a bust is a woman's chest

explanation.surface: A tabloid report of someone kissing a person's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: Smackers are slang for kisses, not money or blows; to buss is an old word for kiss, and its past tense sounds like a chest measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: To buss is an archaic or jocular verb for to kiss, so planting smackers on someone is exactly what it means.

clue.text: Say to a person

blocks.note: for and to both mean towards, as in heading for home
one is a pronoun for a person, as in one must

explanation.surface: An instruction to speak to an individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like a verb of speech but is the definition in its sense 'for example'; the rest builds the phrase in two short words.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Say' introduces an instance, as 'for example' does, and the phrase is used the same way: 'Paris, for one'.

clue.text: Drunken evolutionary bar rant expressed heartfelt feelings

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining the words spoken

indicators.note: bar means except, so those letters are excluded
a drunk staggers about, so the letters are reeling into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A drunken rant in a bar about evolution that ends in emotional confessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, which suits 'Drunken', but it means except. The letters of the rant come out of the long word before the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-word declaration is how people voice deep affection, so it is what someone says expressing tender emotion.

clue.text: Maybe excel with muscle, rippling amount!

indicators.note: rippling means moving in waves, so the letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boast about outdoing others with an impressive amount of rippling muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rippling' belongs with muscle in the surface but works on the next word. 'Maybe' marks the definition as one way of excelling, by force of numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To outman is to surpass an opponent in manpower or manliness, one way of excelling through sheer brawn.

clue.text: Such eliciting notice from potential addressees?

definitions.text: Such eliciting notice from potential addressees?

indicators.note: eliciting draws something out, so these letters are pulled from the word
something potential is not yet in its final form, so the letters can be rearranged

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, a short advertisement
taken as written, then shortened and scrambled

explanation.surface: Letters that would draw a reply from the people they might be sent to.
explanation.walkthrough: Des res is British estate-agent shorthand for a desirable residence. Read whole, the clue says such homes are what get noticed by people who might live at that address.
explanation.definitionFit: Desirable residences attract the eye of house-hunters, who would be the people receiving post at those addresses.

clue.text: One’s first moved to travel on e.g. bus with three conductors?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase defining a noun

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, the only one kept
something moved changes position, so one letter shifts place within the phrase

blocks.note: the opening letter of One, the letter that shifts
to ride is to travel on a bus or similar vehicle

explanation.surface: A bus with three conductors, one of whom moves first.
explanation.walkthrough: Conductors look like bus staff collecting fares, a picture the bus supports, but they are electrical: a triode valve has three electrodes.
explanation.definitionFit: A triode is a thermionic valve with three electrodes, anode, cathode and grid, each one an electrical conductor.

clue.text: Poor school rings out each time for a progress-checker

indicators.note: each ring-shaped letter is taken out and something else put in its place

blocks.note: broke means penniless
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
taken as written, the letter put in

explanation.surface: A failing school tolls its bell every time an inspector arrives to check progress.
explanation.walkthrough: Rings are O-shaped letters; each one in the two words becomes an A. A pod is a group of whales, as a school is of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake pad presses on the disc to slow a vehicle, literally checking its progress in the sense of restraining it.
